correctness.rationale: In the independent equal-rate copying-reset chain, the stationary generator yields Var X_i=iV and Cov(X1,Xj)=V/2^(j−1); the conditional expectation semigroup is exp(t times a lower bidiagonal matrix). Multiplying its exact exponential by stationary source covariances reproduces forward F_n=V2^(−m)e^(−z)Σ_{k=0}^m(2z)^k/k! and reverse R_n=V2^(−m)e^(−z), hence their strict inequality at t>0. Dividing the derivative by its positive last term gives strictly decreasing Q_m(z)=Σ_{j=1}^m(m)_j/(2z)^j, with a unique positive root, not merely a numerical maximum. Uniform bounded-s expansion near z=m of Q_m and the local Stirling formula yield z_m=m−1+O(1/m), Gaussian pulse and maximum Pearson correlation ~sqrt(2/pi)/n. Independently compared lower-bidiagonal matrix exponentials at five depths and five physical lags with closed formulas, and independently bracketed peak roots up to m=100. The infinite Gaussian limit comes from dominated ratios and Stirling, not finite tests.
